title: Giãn giờ làm để giảm cao điểm · Causes / Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some governments are considering encouraging employers to stagger working hours to reduce rush-hour congestion. What difficulties could this policy create, and how could they be addressed?

source.detail: Bài luyện mở rộng biên soạn riêng cho năm 2026. Tham khảo các nhóm chủ đề trong forecast công khai; tình huống, bài mẫu và phân tích được viết mới.
source.disclaimer: Không xác nhận đề này đã xuất hiện hoặc sẽ xuất hiện trong kỳ thi. Các chủ đề ngách được bổ sung để mở rộng phạm vi luyện tập; không gán xác suất ra thi.

keywords: Giãn giờ làm để giảm cao điểm Đường, tàu quá tải khi nhiều người đi đồng thời, dù cùng hạ tầng còn công suất trống ngay trước và sau. Mục tiêu là làm phẳng nhu cầu mà giữ nếp sống khả thi, không đơn thuần chuyển bất tiện từ mạng đường vào gia đình.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.
paragraphs: Governments considering encouraging employers to stagger working hours to reduce rush-hour congestion must address its practical difficulties rather than assuming that the expected benefit guarantees successful implementation. The central implementation difficulty is that uncoordinated changes can disrupt childcare and teamwork, particularly when a worker’s new hours no longer match school schedules or a partner’s employment. Addressing that difficulty requires attention to the specific circumstances of affected users rather than a blanket promise of improvement.

Uncoordinated changes can disrupt childcare and teamwork, particularly when a worker’s new hours no longer match school schedules or a partner’s employment. This difficulty becomes more serious when employers dictate inconvenient shifts to lower-paid staff while retaining preferred schedules for managers, transferring the cost of congestion reduction onto weaker employees. A cleaner asked to start before childcare opens may face a new private transport bill, so an apparently efficient timetable can reduce the benefit of accepting the job.

Participation should be negotiated, supported by adjusted transit frequency and coordinated with care services, with protections against arbitrary or discriminatory scheduling. Negotiation allows staff to identify workable time windows, while coordination with childcare and transport prevents each organisation from optimising its own schedule at everyone else’s expense. Offices near one station could stagger start times after surveying caring commitments, retaining a compatible option for parents whose school arrangements cannot readily change. Employees should retain a way to challenge unequal scheduling, otherwise a formally voluntary programme may become compulsory for people whose bargaining power is weakest.
Staggered hours can ease rush-hour overload, but negotiated schedules and coordinated care arrangements are necessary to keep transport savings from becoming household costs.
